accuracy.evidence: Conventions checked against BBC Bitesize KS3 English (writing a formal letter, writing a script) and the National Literacy Trust guidance: in UK block-layout formal letters the sender's address and date sit top right and the recipient's address on the left; 'Dear Sir or Madam' pairs with 'Yours faithfully' and a named salutation with 'Yours sincerely'; play scripts put the speaker's name and a colon at the left with no speech marks, and actions or delivery in brackets. The adult text notes the US difference ('Sincerely') so the rule is not overstated.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors KS3 teachers report most: keeping speech marks and reporting clauses ('he said') when scripting, pairing 'Dear Sir or Madam' with 'Yours sincerely', writing talk notes as a full speech to read aloud, slang or emojis in a formal register, and chopping prose at random so lines end on 'the' or 'of'. The line-break feedback says 'usually' so it does not ban deliberate enjambment.

lab_distinct.evidence: Distinct from 470 (flagaud, purpose and tone dial): this lab works on the conventions inside each form. It has a fragment-to-form sort read from layout alone, a six-slot letter page filled in order, a salutation-to-sign-off matcher that builds a rule table, a prose extract that re-renders live as each scripting change is applied, and a lineation tool where tapping a word ends a line. The shingle gate passed against all flag labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each task makes the learner apply a convention and see the result: the letter page only fills in the conventional order, the sign-off table records the three rules as they are earned, the script text visibly changes from prose to script with each of the four changes, and the poem re-flows into lines after each accepted break, so the learner sees four lines ending drumming, bus, wait, bell.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions where the wrong options are real beliefs: that describing words signal a script, that your own address goes after your name, that 'Dear Sir or Madam' takes 'Yours sincerely', that scripts use speech marks and 'she said', and that a poem's line can end anywhere. Every reveal restates what the learner just built and names their choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions with fourteen slip tags, each answered with the convention that fixes it, e.g. 'You named Ms Patel, so it is Yours sincerely. Faithfully pairs with Dear Sir or Madam.' and 'Reading out a full script sounds flat and loses eye contact. Notes are short prompts you glance at.' In-lab mistakes (wrong form, out-of-order letter part, wrong sign-off, adding 'she replied', a weak line break) each get a specific explanation.

readability.evidence: Learner text passes the 6.5 FK target with short sentences that define each term on first use (conventions, salutation, register, stage directions, lineation). The adult text passes 9.5 and uses the KS3 programme-of-study vocabulary: form, genre, register, conventions, salutation, sign-off, stage directions, lineation and stanza, plus the Common Core W.6.4 to W.8.4 references.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler scan and the explanation-overlap gate, including against lesson 470 on form and tone. Each learner paragraph covers a different form (overview, letter, script, talk notes and poem), and the adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, the terms and the UK/US sign-off note, the named mistakes and the lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at Android 360 px dark and iPhone 13 light: fragments and the script wrap inside their panels, the letter slots keep the top-right address layout at 360 px, and the sign-off rule table was shortened after it clipped at 360 px. Answer buttons are full lbtn buttons that wrap to new rows, and the poem words can be tapped directly or chosen with 'Break after' buttons.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations and no console errors. Canvas text is drawn in the theme text colour on the theme panel colour, every canvas action has a labelled button twin (e.g. 'Sign off with Yours faithfully', 'End a line after bus'), and the canvas aria-label follows each spoken explanation.
